characterization_methods.key_findings: Fully austenitic matrix of equiaxed, polygonal grains with dark rounded manganese oxide particles on and along grain boundaries and in small clusters.
characterization_methods.purpose: Observe the microstructure of the MIM-processed Fe–22Mn–0.4C–1.5Al–1.5Si steel sintered at 1360 °C for 1 h.

characterization_methods.key_findings: Coarser equiaxed austenitic grains with more pronounced intragranular striations; manganese oxide particles form a thicker, more continuous grain-boundary network.
characterization_methods.purpose: Observe the microstructure of the MIM-processed Fe–22Mn–0.4C–1.5Al–1.5Si steel sintered at 1360 °C for 3 h.

interfaces.phase_evolution: Longer sintering at 1360 °C coarsens the austenitic matrix while leaving and redistributing the manganese oxide second phase along the grain boundaries.

processing_steps.method: mixing of steel powder with HDPE and paraffin wax

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Figure 9 shows the same MIM steel sintered at 1360 °C for 1 h and 3 h.

phases_present.morphology: equiaxed, polygonal grains with fine internal striations
dark, rounded particles sitting on and along grain boundaries and in small clusters
coarser equiaxed, polygonal grains with clearer and more pronounced internal striations
thicker, more continuous network of dark rounded particles along grain boundaries

structures.overall_structure: Fully austenitic structure with equally distributed manganese oxide particles

unmapped_findings: The metal injection molding (MIM) fabrication process was proposed to further improve the wear-resistant properties of Fe–Mn–C–Al low-density steel (b0082).

Following this MIM fabrication method for Fe–22Mn–0.4C–1.5Al–1.5Si steel, ultrahard SiC, alumina, and nitride particles can be mixed with the steel powders to prepare composite materials and further improve wear-resistant properties (b0082).
